why: one discovered endpoint on a topic -- rclcpp's `rclcpp::TopicEndpointInfo`, handed to the visitor of `get_publishers_info_by_topic` / `get_subscriptions_info_by_topic`. `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/graph.hpp:68`. The C++ face of `c:topic_endpoint_info_t`, and it diverges in the same two ways, both with a named constraint. (1) NO ALLOCATOR: rclcpp returns a `std::vector<TopicEndpointInfo>` of `std::string` fields; ours is the ELEMENT of a stream, and its three strings BORROW the backend's own storage for the duration of the visit -- copyable, but a caller that needs a name afterwards copies it into its own `nros::FixedString<N>`. The GID is held by value and does survive a copy. (2) NO QoS ACCESSOR, deliberately, and absent rather than present-and-empty: rclcpp's `qos_profile()` reports the GRANTED profile, no backend behind this API can read a remote's grant back, and zenoh's liveliness token carries the DECLARING side's request rather than a negotiated grant -- so a ported file that asks for it fails to COMPILE instead of reading a QoS nobody granted (RFC-0089: never compile and differ). Cyclone can read a real grant and will need one; adding it then is additive. Its members inherit this verdict.
